x: From nothing to a running console and your first detections. Build AeroProve, create a store and its first administrator, sign in with a passkey, then connect a source, install detections and decide who else may do what. Build it#Go 1.27 or later is the only requirement. There is nothing else to fetch.git clone https://github.com/AeroProve/AeroProve aeroprove && cd aeroprove go build -o aeroprove ./cmd/aeroprove Create a store and its first administrator#./aeroprove init --admin you@example.comIt prints a one-time link that adds that person's passkey and does nothing else. There is no default password and no default account. Start the console and add your passkey#./aeroprove serveThe console listens on 127.0.0.1:8080. Open the link init printed, add a passkey, and you are signed in. Follow Get started#Get started in the console walks four things: bring events in, decide what counts as wrong, know the estate, and decide who else may do what. It reads the store rather than telling a story, so each step is ticked when it is done.

Once anybody is an administrator, a command run from a terminal needs a token, which proves who is running it. Issuing an administrator's token takes a second administrator, so ask for yours, approve it in the console, where Approvals lists it, and collect it within a day: aeroprove token issue you --principal you@example.com --role admin aeroprove pending redeem ID The token is printed once. Keep it in ~/.aeroprove/token, or pass it as VAIGIL_TOKEN or --token. The same first steps, from the terminal: aeroprove vault enable aeroprove connect add okta --org example VAIGIL_CONNECT_SECRET=... aeroprove connect secret okta aeroprove collect run aeroprove detect pack install aeroprove detect run aeroprove estate build aeroprove auth enrol sam@example.com aeroprove auth grant sam@example.com analyst See Connectors and feeds, Detections, Estate and workforce and People for each.
The first screen after signing in is Today: what is waiting for you to decide, then what is wrong in the parts of the estate you work in.
The box in the bar finds a screen or a setting by the words you would use for it. There is no query syntax: every word is looked up, and a colon, a quote or a bracket is part of a word.

Get the program, and run it the way it is meant to be run. Build AeroProve from source with Go alone, install it with make, run it under systemd or in a distroless container, and put it behind a reverse proxy.

Go 1.27 or later, and nothing else: go.mod has no require block, so the standard library and the Go toolchain are the whole build. make sudo make install make install honours prefix and DESTDIR, and sudo make uninstall removes it. Without make: go build -o aeroprove ./cmd/aeroprove install -m 0755 aeroprove /usr/local/bin/

docker build -t aeroprove . docker run --rm -v aeroprove:/srv aeroprove --root /srv/store init --admin you@example.com docker run -p 8080:8080 -v aeroprove:/srv aeroprove The first command prints the link that adds your passkey; open it once the second is running. The image is the binary alone on gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot: no shell, no package manager, no interpreter and no libc. It runs as nonroot and carries LICENSE and NOTICE.

The release workflow publishes a static binary for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, with SHA256SUMS, a build provenance attestation for each, and the image ghcr.io/aeroprove/aeroprove. Check a binary before you run it: sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS gh attestation verify aeroprove-linux-amd64 --repo AeroProve/AeroProve

Set admin.base_url to the address people use and admin.behind_tls_proxy to true. The repository's deploy/ folder has a systemd unit and a Caddy configuration. aeroprove config set admin.base_url https://aeroprove.example.com aeroprove config set admin.behind_tls_proxy true

The terms this manual uses, defined once. Short definitions of the words the AeroProve manual and console use: sources, events, detections, findings, cases, regimes, playbooks, actions, the audit log. SourceWhere events come from: a connector reading another tool's API, a log file mapped by a source mapping, or a feed another system pushes to. EventOne thing that happened, mapped to one shape and kept append-only in the event store before anything reads it. Detection ruleA declared condition over events, with fixtures it must match and must not. A rule is live, in the trial ring (it records what it would raise) or off. FindingSomething a rule, a correlation or an automation says is wrong. Its state is open, triaged, accepted, fixed, stale, false-positive or benign, and every decision on it is kept. Case, incidentA record of something being handled, graded sev1 to sev4, with the notification duties of each regime that applies. RegimeA law with a notification clock: GDPR (eu), NIS2, DORA, SEC, CIRCIA or HIPAA. A clock starts when somebody decides the organisation is aware. PlaybookSteps for a kind of incident, proposed, approved and then worked through step by step. ActionOne declared thing done to another platform, such as suspending an Okta account. Asked for by one person, approved by another. AutomationA rule of the form when this happens, if this is true, do this, in one of three modes: watch, ask or act. EstateThe people who work here and what they use, joined across the tools that know about them. SSVC, VEXSSVC is the decision tree that turns a vulnerability's facts into what to do; VEX is the published statement of whether a product is affected. Audit logThe append-only record of every change AeroProve makes, hash-chained, signed and anchored.

Everything waiting for you to decide, in one place. One screen for everything waiting for you: actions on other platforms, runs an automation held, and privileged changes that need a second administrator. Three things wait for a person, and each is decided by somebody other than whoever asked for it: An action on another platform, asked for on a case. A run an automation held, because its mode is ask. A privileged change: making somebody an administrator, issuing an administrator's token, weakening a setting, lowering how many approvals a change needs, or moving the audit log. aeroprove approvals aeroprove incident act-approve ID N aeroprove automate approve RUN aeroprove pending approve ID What was asked for, by whom and why is shown before anybody decides, and the decision is in the audit log. A privileged change asked for by the only administrator is applied as they make it, and the record says it was approved alone.

One queue, ranked by risk, and every decision kept. One queue of security findings ranked by risk, decisions kept and replayable, and an AI analyst that suggests a verdict from counts without ever recording one. Read the queue#aeroprove finding list --state open aeroprove finding risk aeroprove finding story ID Let the analyst take the first pass#aeroprove analyst plan aeroprove analyst triage --limit 20 --dry-runThe model is any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set with VAIGIL_MODEL_URL, VAIGIL_MODEL_KEY and VAIGIL_MODEL. Without one, findings are triaged by people alone. Decide#aeroprove finding decide ID false-positiveThe states are open, triaged, accepted, fixed, stale, false-positive and benign.

s: What a log line cannot do to the analyst
x: A finding's evidence is log text, written by whoever reached the log. So nothing depends on the model declining an instruction, and the worst a planted line can do is make a suggestion wrong: What it reads, and in what order, is a plan fixed in code. Nothing a log says can add a step. It is given counts and closed words the program worked out, and, separately and marked, the text somebody else wrote. Its answer is one word from a closed set with a confidence, shown only above a threshold. The reason a person reads is assembled from the counts, never from what the model wrote. Personal data and credentials are masked before the prompt leaves and restored in the answer. A person records the verdict; the analyst has no way to. aeroprove analyst eval --k 3 measures it against what people decided.
aeroprove detect replay runs today's rules over the events again and says which decisions would now be different, and aeroprove detect learn FINDING turns a decision into a fixture.

Incidents with the clocks each law starts, and actions a second person approves. Declare incidents with the clocks GDPR, NIS2, DORA, SEC, CIRCIA and HIPAA start, run playbooks, and act on other platforms once a second person approves. Choose the regimes that apply#aeroprove incident regimes eu nis2With none set, a new incident starts with no obligations and no clocks. Declare an incident#aeroprove incident declare --title "Token used from an unknown country" --grade sev2 --finding ID Start the clocks#A clock starts when somebody decides the organisation is aware, and that decision is recorded with its reason.aeroprove incident decide ID aware --because "..." aeroprove incident duties Discharge or waive each duty#aeroprove incident discharge ID "NIS2 early warning" --because "sent to the CSIRT" aeroprove incident waive ID "GDPR Article 34" --because "no personal data involved" Work a playbook#aeroprove incident playbooks aeroprove incident propose ID account-compromise aeroprove incident step ID account-compromise STEP done --because "..."The shipped playbooks cover account compromise, phishing, malware on an endpoint, a lost device and exposed data. Act on another platform, with a second person#aeroprove action add okta-suspend-user --org example aeroprove incident act ID okta-suspend-user okta:USER --because "..." aeroprove incident act-approve ID 1The exact request is shown before anybody approves it, and it is sent only when a second person does. The deadlines are the published ones, counted from the decision, not legal advice. Notices to the people affected are drafted, planned and sent with aeroprove notify.

What happened, kept append-only, and what is rare enough to look at. Every event mapped to one shape and kept append-only, with retention and legal holds, identity links across platforms, and a hunt that shows what is rare.
aeroprove spool stats aeroprove spool verify aeroprove spool retain --apply aeroprove spool hold NAME --why "litigation hold" Retention never deletes what a hold covers, and a hold is lifted by name.
aeroprove identity link okta:00u1abc dana@example.com aeroprove identity list

aeroprove telemetry fields events.jsonl aeroprove hunt --field raw.user_agent --by actor events.jsonl aeroprove triage events.jsonl --rules ./rules A hunt counts one field's values and shows the rarest, which is what is worth a look. The Hunt screen does the same over the store, and offers what you found as the start of a rule.

Indicators of compromise, from STIX 2.1 bundles or plain lists. Import indicators of compromise from STIX 2.1 bundles or plain lists, add them one at a time, and see which events and findings they match. aeroprove intel import bundle.json --source "isac" aeroprove intel add 203.0.113.7 --source "case 12" aeroprove intel list aeroprove intel remove ID A STIX 2.1 bundle's indicators are read from their patterns. A pattern with AND, a time qualifier, a wildcard or a range is reported as not read, never guessed at. A plain list carries one value to a line, defanged or not. Each indicator keeps the source it came from, so a match says who said it was bad, and the events already held are searched for it when it arrives.

Rules with fixtures, Sigma import, a trial ring, and suppressions that end. Write detection rules with fixtures, import Sigma, trial a rule before it reaches the queue, correlate across platforms, and suppress noise with an end date. Install the shipped rules#aeroprove detect pack install aeroprove detect testEach rule carries fixtures it must match and must not, MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs, and a line on what it does not catch. Bring your own, in the open standard#aeroprove sigma import ./rules Trial a rule before it reaches the queue#aeroprove detect ring RULE trial --because "new rule" aeroprove detect stats aeroprove detect ring RULE live --because "a week without a false positive"In the trial ring a rule records what it would raise, and its record earns it the queue. Suppress, until a date#aeroprove detect suppress RULE user.name=svc-backup --owner dana --until 2026-12-31 --because "known job" Correlations raise a finding about several events across rules and platforms, once their window closes; aeroprove correlate demo shows one end to end.

When this happens, do this: rules that watch, ask, or act within limits. Automation rules of the form when this happens, do this, in watch, ask or act mode, with limits, approvals by a second person, and sign-in rules for step-up. aeroprove automate templates aeroprove automate add TEMPLATE aeroprove automate mode ID ask aeroprove automate runs aeroprove automate approve RUN Watch records what the rule would do. Ask waits for a person to approve each run. Act does it at once, within an hourly limit per rule, so one noisy source cannot suspend everybody. Whoever wrote a rule does not approve the runs it holds. Approving a run that acts on people's access takes an administrator of all of AeroProve. Rules about sign-ins can tell an office or a VPN from anywhere else: aeroprove geo network add 198.51.100.0/24 head-office --kind office aeroprove geo status

Read other tools through their APIs, map their logs, and take what they push. Read Okta, Entra ID, GitHub, KnowBe4, Vanta and more through their APIs, map logs from 17 platforms to one shape, and receive SSF, CAEP and webhook feeds.

A connector reads one tool through its API, over only the endpoints its manifest declares, with a credential sealed under AeroProve's keyring. With no keyring, no credential can be stored. aeroprove vault enable aeroprove connect catalogue aeroprove connect add okta --org example aeroprove connect check okta VAIGIL_CONNECT_SECRET=... aeroprove connect secret okta aeroprove connect run okta --save A region is chosen from the connector's own list, never typed as a hostname, so adding a connector cannot point a credential at another machine. The catalogue says which credential each needs and the least it should be allowed to do. Shipped connectors: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub, EVM smart contracts through a Blockscout explorer, KnowBe4, ManageEngine Endpoint Central, ManageEngine MDM Plus and Vanta. aeroprove connect probe shows the shape of a response, never its values.

aeroprove collect run aeroprove collect file aws/cloudtrail trail.json aeroprove collect auto 15m Logs are mapped to one shape from AWS CloudTrail, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Azure, Google Workspace, Google Cloud, Okta, Duo, CrowdStrike Falcon, Jamf Pro, GitHub, Kubernetes, Cloudflare, Salesforce, Slack, Snowflake, Linux auditd and EVM chains. aeroprove source add adds a mapping of your own, checked against a sample, and aeroprove telemetry check says whether what it produces can be used at all.

aeroprove inbound add ssf corp-idp aeroprove inbound add okta okta-hooks aeroprove inbound add webhook ci aeroprove inbound status NAME A feed's endpoint is /feeds/NAME on the console. Shared Signals (SSF, CAEP, RISC) are verified against the transmitter's keys; webhooks against their secret. What arrives is stored like anything collected, and put to the automations as a signal.

Decide vulnerabilities, publish what you decided, and fix the ones that matter. Rank vulnerabilities with CISA KEV and EPSS, decide them with SSVC, publish OpenVEX, scan SBOMs against OSV, import SARIF, and plan upgrades clearing most risk. Import what is known#aeroprove vuln import --bom sbom.json --where api --osv osv.json --kev kev.json --epss epss.csv aeroprove vuln reach --source ./src --where apireach reads the asset's source for the symbols each open advisory names, and records what it found against that advisory. Say what each asset is#aeroprove vuln asset ISSUER:VALUE --exposure open --impact high --because "public API"Exposure is small, controlled or open; impact is low, medium, high or very high. Read the queue and the plan#aeroprove vuln queue aeroprove vuln plan aeroprove vuln why CVE-2026-0001The plan is the smallest set of upgrades that clears the most risk. Decide, and publish#aeroprove vuln assess CVE-2026-0001 PKG not_affected aeroprove vuln accept CVE-2026-0002 PKG --owner dana --until 2027-01-31 --because "..." aeroprove vuln vex --author "Example Ltd" --id https://example.com/vex/1The statuses are affected, fixed, not_affected and under_investigation. A risk acceptance names its owner, its end date and its reason.
aeroprove sca scan --bom sbom.json --osv db.json aeroprove sarif read results.sarif aeroprove appsec triage

Who works here, what they use, how exposed each is, and reminders that close the gaps. Join who works here with their devices, training and accounts across your tools, see where coverage is missing, send reminders, and review vendors and access. aeroprove estate build aeroprove estate scores --limit 20 aeroprove workforce coverage aeroprove workforce gaps aeroprove remind preview aeroprove remind send The estate joins the people your identity provider knows with the devices, training records and accounts other tools report, leavers included. A person's score is a file on an employee, so the Workforce risk screen is for administrators only, and the MCP interface shows only numbers, never names.

aeroprove vendor reconcile aeroprove vendor review ID aeroprove access open q4 identities.jsonl --scope okta,github --due 2026-12-10 aeroprove access decide q4 okta:00u1abc revoke aeroprove access close q4 identities-after.jsonl Each account is kept, revoked or reduced. A review closes on a later import, which shows whether what was decided was done; without one, a revocation is reported as unverified.

Who may do what, granted on a path, ending when it should. Grant roles and jobs on a path, deny what a broader grant would allow, explain any decision, provision people with SCIM, and issue tokens that end. aeroprove auth grant sam@example.com analyst aeroprove auth grant lee@example.com engineer --for 30d aeroprove auth deny sam@example.com responder --on /security/vulns aeroprove auth explain sam@example.com respond aeroprove auth list explain walks every binding and says which one decided, and why the others did not. See Roles for what each role may do.
aeroprove scim token aeroprove scim map security-analysts analyst aeroprove scim status The identity provider adds, changes and removes people; a group is mapped to a role or a job.

aeroprove token issue ci --principal ci-bot aeroprove token list aeroprove token revoke ID aeroprove token stale A token is shown once and stored only as a hash. An administrator's token takes a second administrator.

Four roles in a ladder, three jobs beside it, and the duties kept apart. Four roles in a ladder (viewer, analyst, responder, admin), three jobs beside it (engineer, vuln-manager, auditor), and duties kept apart so nobody acts alone. RoleMay viewerread findings, cases, the vulnerability queue and the dashboards analysttriage findings, open cases and add notes to them, hunt through events responderrun cases, ask for an action on another platform, approve somebody else's action, accept a risk adminmanage people, connectors and their credentials, and settings Each role includes the ones before it. Beside the ladder are jobs, granted for a set time: an engineer tunes detections and automation rules, a vuln-manager decides vulnerabilities, and an auditor reads the queue and the audit log. A job is granted for a set time, and the grant ends by itself. aeroprove auth roles prints the whole model.

An action on another platform is approved by somebody other than whoever asked. Whoever wrote an automation rule does not approve the runs it holds. Making somebody an administrator, issuing an administrator's token, weakening a setting, lowering how many approvals a change needs and moving the audit log each take a second administrator.

OpenID Connect and SAML, counted as two factors only when the provider says so. Sign in through OpenID Connect or SAML. Single sign-on counts as two factors only when the identity provider says it used them, or a passkey is asked for.
aeroprove oidc configure aeroprove oidc check aeroprove oidc status
aeroprove saml presets aeroprove saml add aeroprove saml metadata aeroprove saml list

A sign-in through the identity provider counts as two factors only when the provider says it used them: for OpenID Connect, the amr and acr claims with a recent auth_time; for SAML, the authentication context. When it does not say, AeroProve asks for the person's passkey as well.

Sign in with a passkey that checks it is you, and recover without a password. Sign in with a passkey that checks it is you, add one through a one-time enrolment link, lock out failed sign-ins by place, and recover without a password.
aeroprove auth enrol sam@example.com --for 24h It prints a one-time link that adds that person's passkey and does nothing else. Give it to them the way you would give a key; --revoke ends it.
Every passkey must check it is you, with a PIN, a fingerprint or a face, at registration and at every sign-in (NIST SP 800-63B-4). A security key with no PIN is asked to set one.

Failures lock out the places they come from, not the person: from where you usually sign in, or with your passkey, you still can. After many consecutive failures from anywhere, the method is disabled until the person proves themselves another way or an administrator lets it work again. aeroprove auth unlock sam@example.com

s: When every administrator's way in is lost
x: aeroprove auth recover Break-glass for the operator of the machine, recorded in the audit log.

Every setting, what it does, and why a weaker value needs a second administrator. Every AeroProve setting with what it does and its default. A weaker value needs a recorded reason and a second administrator, and bounds no reason steps past. aeroprove config list aeroprove config explain session.idle aeroprove config set session.idle 30m aeroprove config unset session.idle Every default is the safer value. Setting a weaker one needs --accept-risk and a reason that is recorded, and then goes to a second administrator before it applies. Some settings have hard bounds no reason steps outside, such as the hour NIST SP 800-63B-4 sets for an unused session. SettingWhat it is session.idle, session.maxHow long a session lasts unused (an hour, at most), and at most in all. Anybody who can grant access is signed out after fifteen minutes unused. admin.base_url, admin.behind_tls_proxyThe console's public address, and whether a proxy in front of it ends TLS. network.modeOpen, or offline: refuse every connection that would leave the host. auth.throttle.*When failed sign-ins start to be delayed, and how long a delay grows. security.contactWhere your security team is reached. siem.stream.urlWhere the audit log is sent as it is written. passkey.require_hardware, passkey.authenticatorsWhich authenticators may hold a passkey. token.ttl.default, token.ttl.maxHow long a token lasts by default, and at most.

An append-only, signed, anchored record, and a stream of it to another SIEM. An append-only audit log: a hash chain, a Merkle tree, heads signed with Ed25519 and ML-DSA, anchored to Bitcoin, written by its own process, streamed out. aeroprove auditlog verify aeroprove auditlog show SEQ aeroprove auditlog prove SEQ aeroprove auditlog head --save aeroprove auditlog consistency Every change is a record in a hash chain, with a Merkle tree over it. A tree head is signed with Ed25519 and ML-DSA (post-quantum), and prove gives a receipt anybody can check against a head.

aeroprove auditlog anchor submit aeroprove auditlog anchor upgrade aeroprove auditlog anchor status The head is committed to Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps, so rewriting history is detectable by somebody who never trusted the operator.

aeroprove logd aeroprove logd status Run as its own account, the log writer is the only process that writes the log, so the console cannot rewrite what it recorded. A decision that is nothing but its record is reported as failed when the record cannot be written.

aeroprove config set siem.stream.url https://siem.example.com/ingest aeroprove siem stream key aeroprove siem stream status Batches of OCSF, each following the last exactly, each carrying a signed tree head and an HTTP message signature (RFC 9421), so the receiver can prove nothing was dropped or changed. aeroprove siem ocsf, cef and jsonl export the log as files.

Its own network purposes, sealed credentials, separate log writer and session limits. What AeroProve may connect to and why, credentials sealed in a vault, a separate log writer, two factors for all, session limits and an AI that only suggests.

aeroprove network Every outbound connection is for one declared purpose: an action, anchoring, a connector, mail, the AI analyst's model, the SIEM stream, shared signals, Slack reminders, single sign-on and notice webhooks. An undeclared purpose is refused in every mode, and network.mode offline refuses everything that would leave the host.

aeroprove vault status aeroprove vault rotate A connector's credentials and a feed's secret are sealed under a keyring, so the store's files alone give nobody the values: a lost laptop, a backup on an open bucket, a disposed disk. With no keyring, none can be stored.

Everybody signs in with two factors: a passkey that checks it is them, or single sign-on that says it used two. Failed sign-ins lock out places, not people, and sessions end after an hour unused, fifteen minutes for anybody who can grant access.
The AI analyst and agents over MCP read and propose. Neither can record a decision, approve an action, change who may do what, or reach another platform. See Findings and AI agents over MCP.
Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting for the repository.

Every command, and the flags every command takes. Every AeroProve command, grouped as the console's screens are, and the flags every command takes: --json for machines, --root and --token for identity. aeroprove help Every command takes --json, --root DIR and --token T. With --json, standard output is one JSON document. A token can also come from VAIGIL_TOKEN. Eight operations behind four tools, for an agent that reads and proposes. Connect an AI agent to AeroProve over the Model Context Protocol: eight operations behind four tools, to read findings and propose decisions, never to act. aeroprove mcp --list VAIGIL_TOKEN=... aeroprove mcp The agent interface speaks MCP over standard input and output, as the person whose token it carries, with that person's access and no more. An agent loads only the operations it searches for. OperationWhat it does list_findingsthe finding queue, most urgent first read_findingone finding: why it ranks, its evidence, and what has been decided propose_finding_decisionsuggest a decision on a finding for a person to make incident_statusopen incidents: which clocks are running, late or not started detection_statswhat each rule has been worth, and what the numbers suggest changing vuln_planthe smallest upgrades that clear the most vulnerability risk estate_summaryhow many people are at each level of risk, as numbers, never names findfind a screen by words An agent reading events is reading text an attacker chose, so nothing on this interface changes who may do what, approves an action, or reaches another platform.
